messages.body_plain:
Hi Ethan,

Yes, sampler_CRP is hard to read as it has to account for all sorts of different model code that users might provide. My thought was that you might be able to see the key steps without getting bogged down in that, but I understand if that's tricky.

In any case, I'm not really understanding your question. The algorithm you lay out involves modifying the cluster membership (z) and the cluster parameters (theta).
In the run code, the z is set from `model[[target]]`. Then if you want to change the value of z in the actual model, you can modify `model[[target]]` as you do.  Same thing for theta, which in the run code is (I think) `yparmsClust`. You're modifying that via `model$simulate(yparmsClust)`. If you also need to manually set it, you can do so with syntax such as `model[[yparmsClust]] <<- .... `.

Not sure if that helps. We can continue to iterate.

-chris

On Wed, Aug 17, 2022 at 11:59 AM Ethan <ethanm...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hey Chris,
>
> Admittedly, I found the CRP_sampler a little difficult to read.
>
> The logic was as follows:
> Simulate to obtain a draw from the base measure: theta = (theta_1*, ..., theta_{max_components}*)
> Compute log probability for each cluster from k = 1, ..., max_components, max_components + 1, ..., max_components + naux
> Draw z
> If z corresponds to an existing cluster:
> replace all the parameters back to their original values
> If z corresponds to a new cluster:
> change the value to the index corresponding to the first empty cluster
> Set the parameters for the empty cluster to the draw from part (1)
>
> On Tuesday, August 16, 2022 at 1:42:18 PM UTC-4 Christopher Paciorek wrote:
> > Hi Ethan,
> >
> > I'm not quite understanding. When you call $simulate, that will put values into the model in the node(s) that contain the cluster parameters. And then at the end you are copying from the model to mvSaved, so you are storing the new cluster parameter values. In your code comment you mention the value of a parameter for an index, but isn't this just obtained by looking in the appropriate place in the node(s) containing the cluster parameters?
> >
> > More generally, I think you can follow the logic of what is done in our CRP_sampler.
> >
> > (Note - I'm responding quickly without spending the time to think this through carefully...)
> >
> > -chris
> >
> > On Tue, Aug 16, 2022 at 10:09 AM E A <ethanm...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > Hey Chris,
> > >
> > > I've been hard at work on this implementation, and here is what I have come up with. The remaining piece of the puzzle is storing the values of the parameters for the newly-defined clusters.
> > >
> > > logsumexp <- nimbleFunction(
> > >   run = function(a = double(0), b = double(0)) {
> > >     returnType(double(0))
> > >     m <- max(a, b)
> > >     return( log(exp(a-m) + exp(b-m)) + m )
> > >   }
> > > )
> > >
> > > logsumexp_vec <- nimbleFunction(
> > >   run = function(x = double(1)) {
> > >     returnType(double(0))
> > >     m <- max(x)
> > >     return( m + log(sum(exp(x - m))) )
> > >   }
> > > )
> > >
> > > #' Compute log V_n(t) as in Miller and Harrison
> > > #'
> > > #' @param t number of partitions
> > > #' @param n sample size
> > > #' @param lambda mean hyperparameter for poisson prior on k-1
> > > #' @param gamma dirichlet parameter
> > > #' @param tol tolerance for sum
> > > #' @return computation of log V_n(t)
> > > logvn <- nimbleFunction(
> > >   run = function(
> > >       t      = integer(0)
> > >     , n      = integer(0)
> > >     , lambda = double(0)
> > >     , gamma  = double(0)
> > >     , tol    = double(0, default = 1e-12)
> > >   ) {
> > >     returnType(double(0))
> > >     thresh <- 1.0 - tol     ## the sum decays faster than the poisson CDF
> > >     ## Number of partitions t must be <= n
> > >     if ( t > n )
> > >       return(-Inf)
> > >     a <- 0.0      ## Previous value of log V_n(t)
> > >     c <- -Inf     ## Computation of log V_n(t)
> > >     k <- 1        ## counter for the sum
> > >     p <- 0.0      ## poisson CDF calculation (to be compared with thresh)
> > >     while ( abs(a-c) > tol | p < thresh ) {
> > >       if ( k >= t ) {
> > >         gamma_k <- gamma * k
> > >         a       <- c
> > >         b       <- lgamma(k+1) - lgamma(k-t+1) - lgamma(gamma_k + n) + lgamma(gamma_k) + dpois(k-1, lambda, 1)
> > >         c       <- logsumexp(a, b)
> > >       }
> > >       p <- p + dpois(k-1, lambda, 0)
> > >       k <- k + 1
> > >     }
> > >     return(c)
> > >   }
> > > )
> > >
> > > #' Function to get sizes of clusters
> > > #'
> > > #' @param x vector of cluster membership
> > > #' @param max_components maximum number of components
> > > #'
> > > #' @return a vector giving sizes of clusters whose elements are 1:max_components
> > > getClusterSizes <- nimbleFunction(
> > >   run = function(x = double(1), max_components = integer(0)) {
> > >     returnType(double(1))
> > >     res <- rep(0, max_components)
> > >     n   <- length(x)
> > >     for ( i in 1:n ) {
> > >       res[x[i]] <- res[x[i]] + 1
> > >     }
> > >     return(res)
> > >   }
> > > )
> > >
> > >
> > > #' Nimble list for cluster membership
> > > membershipList <- nimbleList(
> > >   empty = double(1), nonempty = double(1)
> > > )
> > > #' Function to get the indexes of the empty and non-empty clusters
> > > #'
> > > #' @param x an object returned from getClusterSizes
> > > #' @return a list of two elements:
> > > #' \itemize{
> > > #'    \item "nonempty" a vector of cluster indexes that are nonempty
> > > #'    \item "empty" a vector of cluster indexes that are empty
> > > #' }
> > > getClusterIndexes <- nimbleFunction(
> > >   run = function(x = double(1)) {
> > >     res <- membershipList$new()
> > >     returnType(membershipList())
> > >     max_components <- length(x)
> > >     for ( i in 1:max_components ) {
> > >       if ( x[i] > 0 ) {
> > >         res$nonempty <- c(res$nonempty, i)
> > >       } else {
> > >         res$empty <- c(res$empty, i)
> > >       }
> > >     }
> > >     return(res)
> > >   }
> > > )
> > >
> > >
> > > #' Mass function for modified CRP
> > > #'
> > > #' Computes the mass function for the modified CRP of Miller
> > > #'
> > > #' @param x vector giving cluster membership
> > > #' @param size length of x
> > > #' @param lambda parameter for poisson prior on (number of components - 1)
> > > #' @param gamma parameter for Dirichlet prior on membership probability
> > > #' @param tol tolerance for computing log normalizing constant
> > > #' @param log whether to return on log scale
> > > #'
> > > #' @return a scalar giving the mass function for the cluster membership
> > > dMCRP <- nimbleFunction(
> > >   run = function(
> > >       x = double(1)
> > >     , size = integer()
> > >     , lambda = double(0)
> > >     , gamma = double(0)
> > >     , tol = double(0, default = 1e-12)
> > >     , log = integer(0, default = 0)
> > >   ) {
> > >     returnType(double(0))
> > >     classSizes <- getClusterSizes(x, max(x))     ## size of each class
> > >     clustList  <- getClusterIndexes(classSizes)  ## list of empty/nonempty indices
> > >     C <- classSizes[clustList$nonempty]          ## vector giving sizes of each nonempty cluster
> > >     t <- length(C)                               ## number of parts in the partition
> > >     ## Compute log V_n(t)
> > >     log_vn <- logvn(t, length(x), lambda, gamma, tol)
> > >     ## Compute log kernel of mass function
> > >     logK <- 0
> > >     ## Compute lgamma(gamma)
> > >     lgamma_gamma <- lgamma(gamma)
> > >     for ( j in 1:t ) {
> > >       logK <- logK + lgamma(gamma + C[j]) - lgamma_gamma
> > >     }
> > >     if ( log )
> > >       return( logK + log_vn )
> > >     return( exp( logK + log_vn ) )
> > >   }
> > > )
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > > #' Dummy random number generator for MCRP
> > > rMCRP <- nimbleFunction(
> > >   run = function(
> > >       n = integer(0)
> > >     , size = integer(0)
> > >     , lambda = double(0)
> > >     , gamma = double(0)
> > >     , tol = double(0, default = 1e-12)
> > >   ) {
> > >     returnType(double(1))
> > >     return(rep(1, size))
> > >   }
> > > )
> > >
> > > sampler_MFM <- nimbleFunction(
> > >   name = 'sampler_MFM',
> > >   contains = sampler_BASE,
> > >   setup = function(model, mvSaved, target, control) {
> > >     targetElements  <- model$expandNodeNames(target, returnScalarComponents = TRUE)
> > >     n               <- length(targetElements)
> > >     zparms          <- model$getParents(target)
> > >     lambda          <- values(model, zparms[1])[1]   ## Poisson parameter
> > >     gamma           <- values(model, zparms[2])[1]   ## Dirichlet parameter
> > >     ## Get names of parameters for response variable
> > >     yvar            <- model$getDependencies(target, self = FALSE, dataOnly = TRUE, stochOnly = TRUE)
> > >     yparmsNames     <- model$getParents(yvar, stochOnly = TRUE, omit = target)
> > >     yparmsNames     <- model$getVarNames(nodes = yparmsNames)
> > >     ## get number of components in mixture model
> > >     max_components <- 0
> > >     yparmsFixed    <- NULL
> > >     yparmsClust    <- NULL
> > >     for ( i in 1:length(yparmsNames) ) {
> > >       yparmsExpanded <- model$expandNodeNames(yparmsNames[i])
> > >       if ( length(yparmsExpanded) > 1  ) {
> > >         max_components <- max(max_components, length(model$expandNodeNames(yparmsNames[i])) )
> > >         yparmsClust <- c(yparmsClust, yparmsNames[i])
> > >       } else {
> > >         yparmsFixed <- c(yparmsFixed, yparmsNames[i])
> > >       }
> > >     }
> > >     naux  <- control$naux
> > >     if (is.null(control$naux))
> > >       naux <- min(3, max_components)
> > >     if ( naux > max_components )
> > >       stop("Number of auxiliary parameters must be fewer than max number of components.")
> > >     lognaux <- log(naux)
> > >   }
> > >   , run = function() {
> > >     ## Get current cluster membership
> > >     z <- model[[target]]
> > >
> > >     ## Create copy of cluster-specific parameters
> > >     yparmClustCopy <- values(model, yparmsClust)
> > >
> > >     for ( j in 1:n ) {
> > >       ## Remove observation j
> > >       if ( j == 1 ) {
> > >         z_mj <- z[2:n]
> > >       } else if ( j == n ) {
> > >         z_mj <- z[1:(n-1)]
> > >       } else {
> > >         z_mj <- z[c(1:(j-1), (j+1):n)]
> > >       }
> > >       ## number in each cluster after taking away obs j
> > >       clustSize_mj     <- getClusterSizes(z_mj, max_components)  ## cluster sizes
> > >       clustIndexes_mj  <- getClusterIndexes( clustSize_mj )      ## list giving which clusters are empty / non-empty
> > >       clustEmpty_mj    <- clustIndexes_mj$empty                  ## indices of empty clusters
> > >       clustNonempty_mj <- clustIndexes_mj$nonempty               ## indices of non-empty clusters
> > >       k_mj             <- length(clustNonempty_mj)               ## number of filled clusters after taking away obs j
> > >       logProbs_mj_cl   <- rep(-Inf, max_components)              ## placeholder for log likelihood for components
> > >       logProbs_mj_aux  <- rep(-Inf, naux)                        ## placeholder for log likelihood for auxiliary
> > >       log_vn_tplus1    <- logvn(k_mj + 1, n, lambda, gamma)      ## logvn function
> > >       log_vn_t         <- logvn(k_mj, n, lambda, gamma)          ## logvn function
> > >       logalpha_mj      <- log(gamma) + log_vn_tplus1 - log_vn_t  ## log concentration parameter for MFM
> > >       alpha_mj         <- exp(logalpha_mj)                       ## concentration param for MFM
> > >       logden_mj        <- log(n - 1 + alpha_mj)                  ## log denominator for cluster probs
> > >       logProbNew_mj    <- logalpha_mj - lognaux - logden_mj      ## log probability of being in new cluster excluding likelihood
> > >
> > >       ## loop through number of clusters + aux variables
> > >       for ( k in clustNonempty_mj ) {
> > >         ## Temporarily change cluster membership to compute log probability
> > >         model[[target]][j] <- k
> > >
> > >         ## Compute log probability of being in cluster k
> > >         logProbs_mj_cl[k] <- log(clustSize_mj[k]) - logden_mj + model$calculate(yvar[j])
> > >       }
> > >
> > >       ## For auxiliary parameters:
> > >       ##    1. Draw from base measure
> > >       ##    2. Compute log probability for being in new cluster
> > >       model$simulate(yparmsClust)
> > >       for ( k in 1:naux ) {
> > >         ## Temporarily change cluster membership
> > >         model[[target]][j] <- k
> > >
> > >         ## Compute log probability for this cluster
> > >         logProbs_mj_aux[k]  <- logProbNew_mj + model$calculate(yvar[j])  ## add on log likelihood
> > >       }
> > >
> > >       ## Draw new cluster membership
> > >       logProbs <- c(logProbs_mj_cl, logProbs_mj_aux)
> > >       logProbs <- logProbs - logsumexp_vec(logProbs)
> > >       znew_j   <- rcat( n = 1, prob = exp(logProbs) )
> > >
> > >       ## If znew refers to an auxiliary draw...
> > >       if ( znew_j > max_components ) {
> > >         ## If no empty clusters, throw error
> > >         if ( length(clustEmpty_mj) == 0 )
> > >           stop("Need to specify more maximum components")
> > >         ## Otherwise, place in first empty cluster
> > >         znew_j <- clustEmpty_mj[1]
> > >
> > >         ## HELP: need to store new value of parameter for this index; restore values for other clusters
> > >
> > >       }
> > >       model[[target]][j] <<- znew_j
> > >     }
> > >
> > >     ## Add new cluster membership to target
> > >     model$calculate(target)
> > >     model$calculate(yparmsClust)
> > >     nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
> > >     nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = yparmsClust, logProb = TRUE)
> > >   }
> > >   , methods = list(
> > >     reset = function () {
> > >       printMessage <<- TRUE
> > >     }
> > >   )
> > > )
> > >
> > >

messages.subject: Re: Sampling (out of sample) from posterior predictive distribution
messages.subject_clean: Sampling (out of sample) from posterior predictive distribution
messages.body_plain:
Hi Lucas,

Big picture -- you don't need to set up an MCMC for the predictive model. You just need to use `simulate` on the appropriate nodes in `ppSamplerNF`, including any y's that you want to sample from the predictive distribution.

That being said, you could run the MCMC to do the simulation as well, so long as you make sure the only samplers are the predictive samplers that sample the nodes of interest. But in that case you'd still need to make sure that any deterministic parents have their values properly calculated given the values you put into the parameters from the original MCMC, before running the predictive samplers, so I don't think there is any benefit to do that rather than just using `simulate`.

As far as why `s` and `y` don't appear, the 'branch' in 'posterior_predictive_branch' relates to the fact that such samplers sample the target node and all downstream predictive nodes as a group, since there are not downstream data nodes. It's just that the downstream nodes that are sampled are not indicated in the information printed out. E.g., consider this model: y ~ dnorm(theta, 1); theta ~ dnorm(0,1). If you don't set 'y' as data, then the whole thing is predictive and a posterior_predictive_branch sampler would be assigned to theta and would also include conditional sampling of y given the sampled value of theta.

I haven't looked in detail at your code to see why you're getting weird results, but hopefully the above helps you figure it out.

-chris

messages.subject_clean: Setup a sampler's object for each chain ?
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

In a custom sampler I use a matrix generated by some function of mine. This matrix depend on the current values of the model.
Currently I recalculate the matrix at each iteration, which is terribly inefficient (the calculation implies several loops and lots of condition checking...), while I could save the matrix and update only the values that should be updated at some point in the sampler.

My problem is for the initialization of this matrix. Since it depends on the model values, if I just create it in the setup part, it will be initialized with the values used for the model creation and any chain using a different starting point will most likely generate errors.

Is there any way to re-setup a sampler at the beggining of a chain ?
The only thing I can think of otherwise would be to initialize it with only zeros, and check its condition when I need it, and compute it completely if it's full-zeros, which is not a very sexy solution...

Thank you,

Rémi

messages.subject: Re: Setup a sampler's object for each chain ?
messages.subject_clean: Setup a sampler's object for each chain ?
messages.body_plain:
Rémi, perhaps someone on the list will have a better solution for you.  My suggestion here is basically what you suggested - setting a flag (0/1 binary variable) in the setup code to indicate whether the matrix is "initialized".  The flag starts at 0, and the matrix initially is all zeros (or anything else).  Then, when you first use the matrix in the run function, check this flag.  If it's 0, then initialize the matrix (and set the flag to 1).  Also, in the reset method of the sampler, set this flag back to 0, so that on future MCMC chains (perhaps with different initial values in the model), the matrix will be initialized again, using the current values in the model.

A quick code sketch is below.  Hopefully this helps, even if it's not elegant, or maybe someone else will have a better suggestion.

Cheers,
Daniel

my_sampler <- nimbleFunction(
    contains = sampler_BASE,
    setup = function(...) {
        ...
        matrixInitializedFlag <- 0
        matrix <- array(0, c(N, M))
    }
    run = function() {
        ## when the matrix is first used:
        if(matrixInitializedFlag == 0) {
            matrixInitializedFlag <<- 1     ## use double assignment operator <<-
            ## initialize matrix here       ## also use <<- here to assign values into the matrix
            ...
        }
        ...
    }
    methods = list(
        reset = funtion() {
            ...
            matrixInitializedFlag <<- 0     ## use <<- here
        }
    )
)

messages.subject_clean: Calling external script from within nimble model?
messages.body_plain:
Hello All,

I have a somewhat tricky project I am working on that links an integrated population model and integral projection model (ala Plard et al 2019 <https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/ecm.1364>). First, some background and then the tricky integration I could use some guidance on.

Model 1 (IPMpop) is a Bayesian state-space integrated population model. The population I am working on has some demographic data such as estimated population counts, sex ratios, and survival. This model is coded in nimble and uses observed data from the population over the last 25-30 years.

Model 2 (IPMind) is a bio-energetic integral projection model that links individual trait (body  mass and reserve mass) to demographic traits and population size. I am most interested in evaluating the impact of parasites and disease on demographics as mediated by their impact on body condition, so this IPMind is vital. This model is composed of survival, reproduction, growth, and development functions that estimate demographics based on the distribution of body size within the population. The problem is I dont have data for individual body size over time, so this model is based on a simulated initial population, I developed this based on the code of Lachish et al 2020 <https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/10.1086/708723>. In its current form, there are a few scripts that are called from a final "run simulations" script to generate model output.

Model 3 is what I am trying to figure out. Essentially, I want to improve the estimates of population size (n females) produced by the IPMind by modeling them as a function of the data in the Bayesian IPMpop. In theory, I could incorporate the IPMind into the Bayesian population model such that the projection kernel estimates population at each time step. For example, in the code below, M is the projection kernel that is estimated by the four R functions packaged into a single 'bigmatrix' function, zr and zs values are the trait value distributions (ie mesh points in an IPMind) and params are the IPM function parameters. So, population size at time t+1 would be a function of growth, survival and reproduction in time t.

for(i in 1:nYears){
M <-  bigmatrix(zr_values, zs_values, params)
indPopVector[i+1]  <- M$G%*%(M$S*indPopVector[i]) + M$D%*%(M$R*indPopVector[i])
}

So, if that is built into the Bayesian IPMpop model in nimble, I should be able to model that as a function of the observed data with something like this, where ndat is the observed count data.
for(i in 1:nndat){
    ndat[i,2] ~ T(dnorm(indPopVector[i], ndat[i,4]),0,550000) # Truncated normal
  }

In the simplest sense my question is whether it is possible to call external R functions from within a nimble model, or whether all of these would have to be recoded as nimbleFunctions? I have also been looking at the nimbleExternalcall and nimbleRcall functions, but given the complexity of what I have (multiple functions calling multiple scripts that set starting values etc) I am not sure how I'd make that work.

If you've managed to read through to here, thanks! In my mind this seems like it should work, but as I stare into R and try to work out the mechanics of it all I get a bit overwhelmed. Any advice or thoughts will be much appreciated. I am happy to share some code off list if someone really wants to get into the weeds of it with me.

Thanks,
Ben

messages.body_plain:
Hi Ben,

I don't think I have fully absorbed what you are trying to do, but I'm going to give a hasty answer in case it gives you enough.

First, a nimbleRcall really just creates a special wrapper or interface function between nimble and an R function.  That special function is a nimbleFunction, but you don't need to care about that.  The nimbleRcall mechanism is quite general except that inputs and outputs have to be numeric objects.

What I'm thinking might be helpful is to realize that you are free from within the nimbleRcall to manipulate the compiled model, or even the compiled samplers, as you wish.  The scheme in very quick outline would be like this:

myRfun <- function(x) { # From the nimbleRcall below, nimble will pack up the arguments for this function and take the return value. Otherwise it just calls your R function.
  # within this function, go ahead and manipulate cm if you want. e.g.
  cm$z <- x+1 # now this function sticks a wrench in the model by changing the values of x.  better know what you're doing statistically, but the code should work.
  # etc.
}

my_nimbleRcall <- nimbleRcall (myRfun.... etc)

m <- nimbleModel(...)
cm <- compileNimble(m). # This is what is used within myRfun

If you want to reach inside a sampler and, say, change a member variable, I could show you how to do that too.  But an alternative would be to put a nimbleRcall in the sampler and have it potentially get whatever information it needs from the R environment that way.

Again, I'm not quite sure of the complexity you need to solve.  Multiple functions calling multiple scripts doesn't sound like a problem.  You referred to setting starting values -- for what?

HTH.  If not, can you maybe say more about the code mechanics you want (regardless of the modeling intent)?

Perry

Hi Perry,

Thanks a lot for taking a stab at it despite my somewhat unclear questions. After thinking through things a bit more, I realize that there is really just one function I want to call within the nimblecode. I’ve also just finally just come to recognize why the nimble functions, or nimbleRcall are necessary – the R code needs to be compiled into the C language in order to work with the MCMC sampler. Sorry I’m a bit slow on that, I often forget all of the work arounds that are required to get an MCMC sampler working within R.

The one thing I’d like to incorporate into my nimble model is the `bigmatrix` function (code below), everything else just needs to be loaded in to the R environment prior to analysis. This bigmatrix function is a wrapper for the four demographic functions that define the population projections, so these functions would all need to be either written as nimbleFunctions, or translated to a nimbleFunction via nimbleRcall, as would the bigmatrix function itself.

I must admit I am not entirely up to speed on all the clever ways nimble models can be worked with and adapted. While I’ve used nimble for several projects I’ve always simply called the model code through nimbleMCMC rather than through the more adaptable multi-step process. That said, I want the inputs and outputs of this function to interact with different nodes of the model I already have, so I don’t know if it would be possible to call the model from within the nimbleRcall. Though, my understanding of all the details there is admittedly limited.

Thanks,

Ben

#################################################################

# FUNCTION TO CONSTRUCT COMPONENTS OF THE IPM KERNAL

################################################################

bigmatrix<-function(zr.values,zs.values, bigmatrix.params) {

  S <- Surv.fun(zr.values,zs.values, bigmatrix.params["surv_int"],

                  bigmatrix.params["surv_slope"], bigmatrix.params["starvation_ratio"],

                  bigmatrix.params["mean_ostertag"],bigmatrix.params["alfa_surv"],bigmatrix.params["theta_ost"])

  R <- Repro.fun(zr.values,zs.values, bigmatrix.params["zs_threshold_k"], bigmatrix.params["cmax_slope"],

                  bigmatrix.params["veg_energy"],bigmatrix.params["half_sat_val"],

                   bigmatrix.params["steepness"], bigmatrix.params["fat_threshold"],bigmatrix.params["burn_slope"],

                   bigmatrix.params["burn_add_summer"], bigmatrix.params["burn_add_winter"], bigmatrix.params["m_anabolism"],bigmatrix.params["m_catabolism"],

                   bigmatrix.params["breeding_zr_threshold"], bigmatrix.params["neonate_mortality"], params["Veg_max"], params["mean_warbles"],

                   bigmatrix.params["mean_ostertag"],bigmatrix.params["alfa_fecund"],bigmatrix.params["alfa_forage"], bigmatrix.params["insect_harass"],bigmatrix.params["theta_ost"])

  G <- G.fun(zr_50, zs_50,bigmatrix.params["cmax_slope"],bigmatrix.params["half_sat_val"],bigmatrix.params["steepness"],bigmatrix.params["fat_threshold"],bigmatrix.params["veg_energy"],

             bigmatrix.params["burn_slope"], bigmatrix.params["burn_add_summer"], bigmatrix.params["burn_add_winter"],bigmatrix.params["m_anabolism"], bigmatrix.params["m_catabolism"],

             bigmatrix.params["zs_threshold_k"], bigmatrix.params["breeding_zr_threshold"],bigmatrix.params["ZR_to_ReproZ"], bigmatrix.params["ZR_to_ZS"], bigmatrix.params["convert_coef_1"],

             bigmatrix.params["Veg_max"],bigmatrix.params["mean_warbles"],bigmatrix.params["mean_ostertag"],bigmatrix.params["alfa_forage"],bigmatrix.params["insect_harass"],bigmatrix.params["theta_ost"])

  D <- D.fun (zr_50, zs_50, bigmatrix.params["cmax_slope"],  bigmatrix.params["half_sat_val"], bigmatrix.params["steepness"],bigmatrix.params["fat_threshold"],

              bigmatrix.params["veg_energy"],bigmatrix.params["burn_slope"],bigmatrix.params["burn_add_summer"],bigmatrix.params["burn_add_winter"],

              bigmatrix.params["m_anabolism"], bigmatrix.params["m_catabolism"], bigmatrix.params["ReproZ_to_OffspringZS"], bigmatrix.params["convert_coef_2"],

              bigmatrix.params["ZR_to_ReproZ"], bigmatrix.params["convert_coef_3"], bigmatrix.params["Veg_max"],

              bigmatrix.params["mean_warbles"],bigmatrix.params["mean_ostertag"],bigmatrix.params["alfa_forage"], bigmatrix.params["insect_harass"],bigmatrix.params["theta_ost"])

  return(list(S=S,R=R,G=G,D=D))

}

messages.body_plain:
My understanding of Neal Algorithm 8 is that you need to compute the log probability of being in an existing cluster as well as a new cluster.

The probability of being in an existing cluster is computed using the parameters of that cluster. To that end, the idea was to *temporarily* change cluster membership and compute the log probability based on being in each cluster.

The probability of being in a new cluster involves (1) drawing parameters from the base measure and (2) computing the probability of being in that cluster. To this end, I:
Drew from the base measure for all clusters by replacing the values in the current cluster parameters (only using the first naux clusters)
Computed the log probability of being in each of the naux cluster based on (1)
So far, this should give me Kmax + naux log probabilities, where Kmax = max number of components to consider and naux = number of auxiliary variables.

Now, if a subject belongs to an existing cluster, I want to revert all parameters back to their initial values (i.e., before the draw from the base measure).

If a subject belongs to a new cluster, I need to update the parameters so that ONLY the value corresponding to the new cluster is changed. This is the part that I am struggling to figure out.

> > > On Tue, Aug 16, 2022 at 10:09 AM E A <ethanm...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > Hey Chris,
> > > >
> > > > I've been hard at work on this implementation, and here is what I have come up with. The remaining piece of the puzzle is storing the values of the parameters for the newly-defined clusters.
> > > >
> > > > logsumexp <- nimbleFunction(
> > > >   run = function(a = double(0), b = double(0)) {
> > > >     returnType(double(0))
> > > >     m <- max(a, b)
> > > >     return( log(exp(a-m) + exp(b-m)) + m )
> > > >   }
> > > > )
> > > >
> > > > logsumexp_vec <- nimbleFunction(
> > > >   run = function(x = double(1)) {
> > > >     returnType(double(0))
> > > >     m <- max(x)
> > > >     return( m + log(sum(exp(x - m))) )
> > > >   }
> > > > )
> > > >
> > > > #' Compute log V_n(t) as in Miller and Harrison
> > > > #'
> > > > #' @param t number of partitions
> > > > #' @param n sample size
> > > > #' @param lambda mean hyperparameter for poisson prior on k-1
> > > > #' @param gamma dirichlet parameter
> > > > #' @param tol tolerance for sum
> > > > #' @return computation of log V_n(t)
> > > > logvn <- nimbleFunction(
> > > >   run = function(
> > > >       t      = integer(0)
> > > >     , n      = integer(0)
> > > >     , lambda = double(0)
> > > >     , gamma  = double(0)
> > > >     , tol    = double(0, default = 1e-12)
> > > >   ) {
> > > >     returnType(double(0))
> > > >     thresh <- 1.0 - tol     ## the sum decays faster than the poisson CDF
> > > >     ## Number of partitions t must be <= n
> > > >     if ( t > n )
> > > >       return(-Inf)
> > > >     a <- 0.0      ## Previous value of log V_n(t)
> > > >     c <- -Inf     ## Computation of log V_n(t)
> > > >     k <- 1        ## counter for the sum
> > > >     p <- 0.0      ## poisson CDF calculation (to be compared with thresh)
> > > >     while ( abs(a-c) > tol | p < thresh ) {
> > > >       if ( k >= t ) {
> > > >         gamma_k <- gamma * k
> > > >         a       <- c
> > > >         b       <- lgamma(k+1) - lgamma(k-t+1) - lgamma(gamma_k + n) + lgamma(gamma_k) + dpois(k-1, lambda, 1)
> > > >         c       <- logsumexp(a, b)
> > > >       }
> > > >       p <- p + dpois(k-1, lambda, 0)
> > > >       k <- k + 1
> > > >     }
> > > >     return(c)
> > > >   }
> > > > )
> > > >
> > > > #' Function to get sizes of clusters
> > > > #'
> > > > #' @param x vector of cluster membership
> > > > #' @param max_components maximum number of components
> > > > #'
> > > > #' @return a vector giving sizes of clusters whose elements are 1:max_components
> > > > getClusterSizes <- nimbleFunction(
> > > >   run = function(x = double(1), max_components = integer(0)) {
> > > >     returnType(double(1))
> > > >     res <- rep(0, max_components)
> > > >     n   <- length(x)
> > > >     for ( i in 1:n ) {
> > > >       res[x[i]] <- res[x[i]] + 1
> > > >     }
> > > >     return(res)
> > > >   }
> > > > )
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > #' Nimble list for cluster membership
> > > > membershipList <- nimbleList(
> > > >   empty = double(1), nonempty = double(1)
> > > > )
> > > > #' Function to get the indexes of the empty and non-empty clusters
> > > > #'
> > > > #' @param x an object returned from getClusterSizes
> > > > #' @return a list of two elements:
> > > > #' \itemize{
> > > > #'    \item "nonempty" a vector of cluster indexes that are nonempty
> > > > #'    \item "empty" a vector of cluster indexes that are empty
> > > > #' }
> > > > getClusterIndexes <- nimbleFunction(
> > > >   run = function(x = double(1)) {
> > > >     res <- membershipList$new()
> > > >     returnType(membershipList())
> > > >     max_components <- length(x)
> > > >     for ( i in 1:max_components ) {
> > > >       if ( x[i] > 0 ) {
> > > >         res$nonempty <- c(res$nonempty, i)
> > > >       } else {
> > > >         res$empty <- c(res$empty, i)
> > > >       }
> > > >     }
> > > >     return(res)
> > > >   }
> > > > )
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > #' Mass function for modified CRP
> > > > #'
> > > > #' Computes the mass function for the modified CRP of Miller
> > > > #'
> > > > #' @param x vector giving cluster membership
> > > > #' @param size length of x
> > > > #' @param lambda parameter for poisson prior on (number of components - 1)
> > > > #' @param gamma parameter for Dirichlet prior on membership probability
> > > > #' @param tol tolerance for computing log normalizing constant
> > > > #' @param log whether to return on log scale
> > > > #'
> > > > #' @return a scalar giving the mass function for the cluster membership
> > > > dMCRP <- nimbleFunction(
> > > >   run = function(
> > > >       x = double(1)
> > > >     , size = integer()
> > > >     , lambda = double(0)
> > > >     , gamma = double(0)
> > > >     , tol = double(0, default = 1e-12)
> > > >     , log = integer(0, default = 0)
> > > >   ) {
> > > >     returnType(double(0))
> > > >     classSizes <- getClusterSizes(x, max(x))     ## size of each class
> > > >     clustList  <- getClusterIndexes(classSizes)  ## list of empty/nonempty indices
> > > >     C <- classSizes[clustList$nonempty]          ## vector giving sizes of each nonempty cluster
> > > >     t <- length(C)                               ## number of parts in the partition
> > > >     ## Compute log V_n(t)
> > > >     log_vn <- logvn(t, length(x), lambda, gamma, tol)
> > > >     ## Compute log kernel of mass function
> > > >     logK <- 0
> > > >     ## Compute lgamma(gamma)
> > > >     lgamma_gamma <- lgamma(gamma)
> > > >     for ( j in 1:t ) {
> > > >       logK <- logK + lgamma(gamma + C[j]) - lgamma_gamma
> > > >     }
> > > >     if ( log )
> > > >       return( logK + log_vn )
> > > >     return( exp( logK + log_vn ) )
> > > >   }
> > > > )
> > > >
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > #' Dummy random number generator for MCRP
> > > > rMCRP <- nimbleFunction(
> > > >   run = function(
> > > >       n = integer(0)
> > > >     , size = integer(0)
> > > >     , lambda = double(0)
> > > >     , gamma = double(0)
> > > >     , tol = double(0, default = 1e-12)
> > > >   ) {
> > > >     returnType(double(1))
> > > >     return(rep(1, size))
> > > >   }
> > > > )
> > > >
> > > > sampler_MFM <- nimbleFunction(
> > > >   name = 'sampler_MFM',
> > > >   contains = sampler_BASE,
> > > >   setup = function(model, mvSaved, target, control) {
> > > >     targetElements  <- model$expandNodeNames(target, returnScalarComponents = TRUE)
> > > >     n               <- length(targetElements)
> > > >     zparms          <- model$getParents(target)
> > > >     lambda          <- values(model, zparms[1])[1]   ## Poisson parameter
> > > >     gamma           <- values(model, zparms[2])[1]   ## Dirichlet parameter
> > > >     ## Get names of parameters for response variable
> > > >     yvar            <- model$getDependencies(target, self = FALSE, dataOnly = TRUE, stochOnly = TRUE)
> > > >     yparmsNames     <- model$getParents(yvar, stochOnly = TRUE, omit = target)
> > > >     yparmsNames     <- model$getVarNames(nodes = yparmsNames)
> > > >     ## get number of components in mixture model
> > > >     max_components <- 0
> > > >     yparmsFixed    <- NULL
> > > >     yparmsClust    <- NULL
> > > >     for ( i in 1:length(yparmsNames) ) {
> > > >       yparmsExpanded <- model$expandNodeNames(yparmsNames[i])
> > > >       if ( length(yparmsExpanded) > 1  ) {
> > > >         max_components <- max(max_components, length(model$expandNodeNames(yparmsNames[i])) )
> > > >         yparmsClust <- c(yparmsClust, yparmsNames[i])
> > > >       } else {
> > > >         yparmsFixed <- c(yparmsFixed, yparmsNames[i])
> > > >       }
> > > >     }
> > > >     naux  <- control$naux
> > > >     if (is.null(control$naux))
> > > >       naux <- min(3, max_components)
> > > >     if ( naux > max_components )
> > > >       stop("Number of auxiliary parameters must be fewer than max number of components.")
> > > >     lognaux <- log(naux)
> > > >   }
> > > >   , run = function() {
> > > >     ## Get current cluster membership
> > > >     z <- model[[target]]
> > > >
> > > >     ## Create copy of cluster-specific parameters
> > > >     yparmClustCopy <- values(model, yparmsClust)
> > > >
> > > >     for ( j in 1:n ) {
> > > >       ## Remove observation j
> > > >       if ( j == 1 ) {
> > > >         z_mj <- z[2:n]
> > > >       } else if ( j == n ) {
> > > >         z_mj <- z[1:(n-1)]
> > > >       } else {
> > > >         z_mj <- z[c(1:(j-1), (j+1):n)]
> > > >       }
> > > >       ## number in each cluster after taking away obs j
> > > >       clustSize_mj     <- getClusterSizes(z_mj, max_components)  ## cluster sizes
> > > >       clustIndexes_mj  <- getClusterIndexes( clustSize_mj )      ## list giving which clusters are empty / non-empty
> > > >       clustEmpty_mj    <- clustIndexes_mj$empty                  ## indices of empty clusters
> > > >       clustNonempty_mj <- clustIndexes_mj$nonempty               ## indices of non-empty clusters
> > > >       k_mj             <- length(clustNonempty_mj)               ## number of filled clusters after taking away obs j
> > > >       logProbs_mj_cl   <- rep(-Inf, max_components)              ## placeholder for log likelihood for components
> > > >       logProbs_mj_aux  <- rep(-Inf, naux)                        ## placeholder for log likelihood for auxiliary
> > > >       log_vn_tplus1    <- logvn(k_mj + 1, n, lambda, gamma)      ## logvn function
> > > >       log_vn_t         <- logvn(k_mj, n, lambda, gamma)          ## logvn function
> > > >       logalpha_mj      <- log(gamma) + log_vn_tplus1 - log_vn_t  ## log concentration parameter for MFM
> > > >       alpha_mj         <- exp(logalpha_mj)                       ## concentration param for MFM
> > > >       logden_mj        <- log(n - 1 + alpha_mj)                  ## log denominator for cluster probs
> > > >       logProbNew_mj    <- logalpha_mj - lognaux - logden_mj      ## log probability of being in new cluster excluding likelihood
> > > >
> > > >       ## loop through number of clusters + aux variables
> > > >       for ( k in clustNonempty_mj ) {
> > > >         ## Temporarily change cluster membership to compute log probability
> > > >         model[[target]][j] <- k
> > > >
> > > >         ## Compute log probability of being in cluster k
> > > >         logProbs_mj_cl[k] <- log(clustSize_mj[k]) - logden_mj + model$calculate(yvar[j])
> > > >       }
> > > >
> > > >       ## For auxiliary parameters:
> > > >       ##    1. Draw from base measure
> > > >       ##    2. Compute log probability for being in new cluster
> > > >       model$simulate(yparmsClust)
> > > >       for ( k in 1:naux ) {
> > > >         ## Temporarily change cluster membership
> > > >         model[[target]][j] <- k
> > > >
> > > >         ## Compute log probability for this cluster
> > > >         logProbs_mj_aux[k]  <- logProbNew_mj + model$calculate(yvar[j])  ## add on log likelihood
> > > >       }
> > > >
> > > >       ## Draw new cluster membership
> > > >       logProbs <- c(logProbs_mj_cl, logProbs_mj_aux)
> > > >       logProbs <- logProbs - logsumexp_vec(logProbs)
> > > >       znew_j   <- rcat( n = 1, prob = exp(logProbs) )
> > > >
> > > >       ## If znew refers to an auxiliary draw...
> > > >       if ( znew_j > max_components ) {
> > > >         ## If no empty clusters, throw error
> > > >         if ( length(clustEmpty_mj) == 0 )
> > > >           stop("Need to specify more maximum components")
> > > >         ## Otherwise, place in first empty cluster
> > > >         znew_j <- clustEmpty_mj[1]
> > > >
> > > >         ## HELP: need to store new value of parameter for this index; restore values for other clusters
> > > >
> > > >       }
> > > >       model[[target]][j] <<- znew_j
> > > >     }
> > > >
> > > >     ## Add new cluster membership to target
> > > >     model$calculate(target)
> > > >     model$calculate(yparmsClust)
> > > >     nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
> > > >     nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = yparmsClust, logProb = TRUE)
> > > >   }
> > > >   , methods = list(
> > > >     reset = function () {
> > > >       printMessage <<- TRUE
> > > >     }
> > > >   )
> > > > )
> > > >
> > > >

messages.body_plain:
One trade-off I am discovering with the above code is that because it uses the base function 'CModelMCMC$run' to allow resumption of sampling after checking convergence, I can't thin the samples as I go. I can thin after recovering the samples to save hard drive space, but the primary sampler does not allow thinning (or burn-in), which means that I end up running out of RAM before I reach convergence. For the time being, it seems like this code is useful at the initial stage of exploring a model, but once I have a sense of how long I'm going to need to run the sampler to get to convergence, I am probably going to have to switch to using the higher level 'nimbleMCMC' function, so that I can implement burn-in and thinning for better memory management.

It might be nice for future versions of NIMBLE if either thinning/burn-in could be included in the base function (...$run) or if an option for resuming sampling could be incorporated into higher level functions that also allow thinning and burn-in.

> Hello all. I realize this is an older post, but thought I'd share that I was able to successfully build on Adrian's code. The code below implements parallel processing, checks Rhats for specified parameters, and if they are too low, it keeps resuming until Rhats meet the desired threshold. The calculation of Rhats leverages the 'mcmcOutput' package. Perhaps others may find this useful.
>
>     #~~~~~~~~~Parallel processing code (won't work in Windows)~~~~~~~~~#
>     library(parallel)
>     library(coda)
>     set.seed(3)
>     cl<-makeCluster(nc, timeout = 5184000)
>     clusterExport(cl, c("model", "inits", "data", "constants", "parameters", "ni"))
>
>     for (j in seq_along(cl)) {
>       set.seed(j)
>       init <- inits()
>       clusterExport(cl[j], "init")
>     }
>     out1 <- clusterEvalQ(cl, {
>       library(nimble)
>       library(coda)
>       model <- nimbleModel(code = model, name = "model",
>
>                            constants = constants, data = data,
>
>                            inits = init)
>       Cmodel <- compileNimble(model)
>       modelConf <- configureMCMC(model)
>       modelConf$addMonitors(parameters)
>
>       modelMCMC <- buildMCMC(modelConf)
>       CmodelMCMC <- compileNimble(modelMCMC, project = model)
>       CmodelMCMC$run(ni, reset = FALSE)
>       return(as.mcmc(as.matrix(CmodelMCMC$mvSamples)))
>     })
>
>     ## Check convergence ##
>     out2 <- out1
>     out2[[1]] <- out2[[1]][seq(nb+2, ni+1, by = nt),]
>     out2[[2]] <- out2[[2]][seq(nb+2, ni+1, by = nt),]
>     out.mcmc <- coda::as.mcmc.list(lapply(out2, coda::as.mcmc))
>     #traceplot(out.mcmc[, "b"])
>     library(mcmcOutput)
>     #if(nc > 1) mod.raw <- coda::as.mcmc.list(lapply(out$samples, coda::mcmc))
>     mod <- mcmcOutput(out.mcmc)
>     sumTab <- summary(mod, MCEpc = F, Rhat = T, n.eff = T, f = T, overlap0 = T, verbose = F)
>     sumTab <- sumTab %>%
>       as_tibble() %>%
>       mutate(Parameter = row.names(sumTab)) %>%
>       select(Parameter, mean:f)
>     #MCMCvis::MCMCtrace(out.mcmc, params = "DELTA1[114, 2]", pdf = F, ISB = F)
>     ind.Rht <- which(!str_detect(sumTab$Parameter, "test.n") &
>                        !str_detect(sumTab$Parameter, "M.save") &
>                        !str_detect(sumTab$Parameter, "pXtheta") &
>                        !str_detect(sumTab$Parameter, "Ind") &
>                        !str_detect(sumTab$Parameter, "ind"))
>     mxRht <- sumTab %>% slice(ind.Rht) %>% pull(Rhat) %>% max(na.rm = T)
>     #sumTab %>% slice(ind.Rht) %>% arrange(desc(Rhat)) %>% View()
>
>
>     ## If has not converged, continue sampling
>     n.reruns <- 0
>     while(round(mxRht, digits = 1) > 1.1) {
>       out2 <- clusterEvalQ(cl, {
>         CmodelMCMC$run(ni, reset = FALSE)
>         return(as.mcmc(as.matrix(CmodelMCMC$mvSamples)))
>       })
>
>       n.reruns <- n.reruns + 1
>       print(str_c("Reruns = ", n.reruns))
>       if(n.reruns == 1) {
>         nb2 <- nb + nb
>         ni2 <- ni + ni
>       } else {
>         nb2 <- nb2 + nb
>         ni2 <- ni2 + ni
>       }
>       out2[[1]] <- out2[[1]][seq(nb2+2, ni2+1, by = nt),]
>       out2[[2]] <- out2[[2]][seq(nb2+2, ni2+1, by = nt),]
>       out.mcmc.update <- coda::as.mcmc.list(lapply(out2, coda::as.mcmc))
>

>       sumTab <- summary(mod, MCEpc = F, Rhat = T, n.eff = T, f = T, overlap0 = T, verbose = F)

> On Thursday, January 20, 2022 at 2:57:06 PM UTC-7 christophe...@gmail.com wrote:
> > hi Dan,
> >
> > Thanks for commenting here.
> >
> > I've checked the example and I do get reproducible results using the code provided. I'm wondering if you modified it such that you are creating random initial values? If so, you'd need to use set.seed before you generate the initial values within the run_MCMC_allcode function.
> >
> > One other note is that the approach in that example relies on simply setting different seeds for the different chains. While this is probably safe, it is possible that the random numbers generated for one chain could partially overlap the random numbers generated for another chain. Even if this happened, I don't think it would cause substantive dependence between the chains. But your approach of using clusterSetRNGStream has the nice feature of ensuring the sequences of random numbers for each of the worker processes won't overlap.
> >
> > -chris
> >
> > On Tue, Jan 18, 2022 at 11:36 AM Daniel Eacker <taurusw...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > Hi,
> > >
> > > A bit late to add this, but I just wanted to add that I don't think this is correct for setting the seed in parallel processing using the parallel package:
> > >
> > > 1) In the `parLapply` call, the values of `X` are the values used for
> > > the `seed` function. So it is used.
> > >
> > > I've tried this and it produces different results across MCMC simulations.
> > >
> > > What I've found that works for repeatable results using parallel processing is to add this just after making the cluster:
> > >
> > > e.g.,
> > >
> > > this_cluster <- makeCluster(2)

messages.subject_clean: Run parallel chains and update model
messages.body_plain:
Quresh, just set the thinning interval in the MCMC configuration object (using conf$setThin(INTERVAL), I believe), doing that before you build and compile the MCMC.  Then, even using mcmc$run(ITERATIONS) will respect the thinning interval, and only record those samples internally.

On Tue, Aug 23, 2022 at 12:17 PM Quresh Latif <quresh...@birdconservancy.org> wrote:

> One trade-off I am discovering with the above code is that because it uses the base function 'CModelMCMC$run' to allow resumption of sampling after checking convergence, I can't thin the samples as I go. I can thin after recovering the samples to save hard drive space, but the primary sampler does not allow thinning (or burn-in), which means that I end up running out of RAM before I reach convergence. For the time being, it seems like this code is useful at the initial stage of exploring a model, but once I have a sense of how long I'm going to need to run the sampler to get to convergence, I am probably going to have to switch to using the higher level 'nimbleMCMC' function, so that I can implement burn-in and thinning for better memory management.
>
> It might be nice for future versions of NIMBLE if either thinning/burn-in could be included in the base function (...$run) or if an option for resuming sampling could be incorporated into higher level functions that also allow thinning and burn-in.
>
> On Monday, August 15, 2022 at 11:23:43 AM UTC-6 Quresh Latif wrote:
> > Hello all. I realize this is an older post, but thought I'd share that I was able to successfully build on Adrian's code. The code below implements parallel processing, checks Rhats for specified parameters, and if they are too low, it keeps resuming until Rhats meet the desired threshold. The calculation of Rhats leverages the 'mcmcOutput' package. Perhaps others may find this useful.
> >
> >     #~~~~~~~~~Parallel processing code (won't work in Windows)~~~~~~~~~#
> >     library(parallel)
> >     library(coda)
> >     set.seed(3)
> >     cl<-makeCluster(nc, timeout = 5184000)
> >     clusterExport(cl, c("model", "inits", "data", "constants", "parameters", "ni"))
> >
> >     for (j in seq_along(cl)) {
> >       set.seed(j)
> >       init <- inits()
> >       clusterExport(cl[j], "init")
> >     }
> >     out1 <- clusterEvalQ(cl, {
> >       library(nimble)
> >       library(coda)
> >       model <- nimbleModel(code = model, name = "model",
> >
> >                            constants = constants, data = data,
> >
> >                            inits = init)
> >       Cmodel <- compileNimble(model)
> >       modelConf <- configureMCMC(model)
> >       modelConf$addMonitors(parameters)
> >
> >       modelMCMC <- buildMCMC(modelConf)
> >       CmodelMCMC <- compileNimble(modelMCMC, project = model)
> >       CmodelMCMC$run(ni, reset = FALSE)
> >       return(as.mcmc(as.matrix(CmodelMCMC$mvSamples)))
> >     })
> >
> >     ## Check convergence ##
> >     out2 <- out1
> >     out2[[1]] <- out2[[1]][seq(nb+2, ni+1, by = nt),]
> >     out2[[2]] <- out2[[2]][seq(nb+2, ni+1, by = nt),]
> >     out.mcmc <- coda::as.mcmc.list(lapply(out2, coda::as.mcmc))
> >     #traceplot(out.mcmc[, "b"])
> >     library(mcmcOutput)
> >     #if(nc > 1) mod.raw <- coda::as.mcmc.list(lapply(out$samples, coda::mcmc))
> >     mod <- mcmcOutput(out.mcmc)
> >     sumTab <- summary(mod, MCEpc = F, Rhat = T, n.eff = T, f = T, overlap0 = T, verbose = F)
> >     sumTab <- sumTab %>%
> >       as_tibble() %>%
> >       mutate(Parameter = row.names(sumTab)) %>%
> >       select(Parameter, mean:f)
> >     #MCMCvis::MCMCtrace(out.mcmc, params = "DELTA1[114, 2]", pdf = F, ISB = F)
> >     ind.Rht <- which(!str_detect(sumTab$Parameter, "test.n") &
> >                        !str_detect(sumTab$Parameter, "M.save") &
> >                        !str_detect(sumTab$Parameter, "pXtheta") &
> >                        !str_detect(sumTab$Parameter, "Ind") &
> >                        !str_detect(sumTab$Parameter, "ind"))
> >     mxRht <- sumTab %>% slice(ind.Rht) %>% pull(Rhat) %>% max(na.rm = T)
> >     #sumTab %>% slice(ind.Rht) %>% arrange(desc(Rhat)) %>% View()
> >
> >
> >     ## If has not converged, continue sampling
> >     n.reruns <- 0
> >     while(round(mxRht, digits = 1) > 1.1) {
> >       out2 <- clusterEvalQ(cl, {
> >         CmodelMCMC$run(ni, reset = FALSE)
> >         return(as.mcmc(as.matrix(CmodelMCMC$mvSamples)))
> >       })
> >
> >       n.reruns <- n.reruns + 1
> >       print(str_c("Reruns = ", n.reruns))
> >       if(n.reruns == 1) {
> >         nb2 <- nb + nb
> >         ni2 <- ni + ni
> >       } else {
> >         nb2 <- nb2 + nb
> >         ni2 <- ni2 + ni
> >       }
> >       out2[[1]] <- out2[[1]][seq(nb2+2, ni2+1, by = nt),]
> >       out2[[2]] <- out2[[2]][seq(nb2+2, ni2+1, by = nt),]
> >       out.mcmc.update <- coda::as.mcmc.list(lapply(out2, coda::as.mcmc))
> >
> >       mod <- mcmcOutput(out.mcmc.update)
> >       sumTab <- summary(mod, MCEpc = F, Rhat = T, n.eff = T, f = T, overlap0 = T, verbose = F)
> >       sumTab <- sumTab %>%
> >         as_tibble() %>%
> >         mutate(Parameter = row.names(sumTab)) %>%
> >         select(Parameter, mean:f)
> >       #MCMCvis::MCMCtrace(out.mcmc, params = "DELTA1[114, 2]", pdf = F, ISB = F)
> >       mxRht <- sumTab %>% slice(ind.Rht) %>% pull(Rhat) %>% max(na.rm = T)
> >       gc(verbose = F)
> >     }
> >     #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#

messages.body_plain:
Ah, perfect! Thanks for pointing that out. I also see that you can set thinning when actually configuring the MCMC using the 'thin' argument (e.g., configureMCMC(Rmodel, thin = 10)). I don't see an argument for setting burn-in, but maybe I'm missing it? In any case, the option for setting thinning in the primary sampler is going to help a lot. Thank you!

On Tuesday, August 23, 2022 at 10:24:59 AM UTC-6 db...@williams.edu wrote:
> Quresh, just set the thinning interval in the MCMC configuration object (using conf$setThin(INTERVAL), I believe), doing that before you build and compile the MCMC.  Then, even using mcmc$run(ITERATIONS) will respect the thinning interval, and only record those samples internally.
>
> On Tue, Aug 23, 2022 at 12:17 PM Quresh Latif <quresh...@birdconservancy.org> wrote:
> > One trade-off I am discovering with the above code is that because it uses the base function 'CModelMCMC$run' to allow resumption of sampling after checking convergence, I can't thin the samples as I go. I can thin after recovering the samples to save hard drive space, but the primary sampler does not allow thinning (or burn-in), which means that I end up running out of RAM before I reach convergence. For the time being, it seems like this code is useful at the initial stage of exploring a model, but once I have a sense of how long I'm going to need to run the sampler to get to convergence, I am probably going to have to switch to using the higher level 'nimbleMCMC' function, so that I can implement burn-in and thinning for better memory management.
> >
> > It might be nice for future versions of NIMBLE if either thinning/burn-in could be included in the base function (...$run) or if an option for resuming sampling could be incorporated into higher level functions that also allow thinning and burn-in.
> >
> > On Monday, August 15, 2022 at 11:23:43 AM UTC-6 Quresh Latif wrote:
> > > Hello all. I realize this is an older post, but thought I'd share that I was able to successfully build on Adrian's code. The code below implements parallel processing, checks Rhats for specified parameters, and if they are too low, it keeps resuming until Rhats meet the desired threshold. The calculation of Rhats leverages the 'mcmcOutput' package. Perhaps others may find this useful.
> > >
> > >     #~~~~~~~~~Parallel processing code (won't work in Windows)~~~~~~~~~#
> > >     library(parallel)
> > >     library(coda)
> > >     set.seed(3)
> > >     cl<-makeCluster(nc, timeout = 5184000)
> > >     clusterExport(cl, c("model", "inits", "data", "constants", "parameters", "ni"))
> > >
> > >     for (j in seq_along(cl)) {
> > >       set.seed(j)
> > >       init <- inits()
> > >       clusterExport(cl[j], "init")
> > >     }
> > >     out1 <- clusterEvalQ(cl, {
> > >       library(nimble)
> > >       library(coda)
> > >       model <- nimbleModel(code = model, name = "model",
> > >
> > >                            constants = constants, data = data,
> > >
> > >                            inits = init)
> > >       Cmodel <- compileNimble(model)
> > >       modelConf <- configureMCMC(model)
> > >       modelConf$addMonitors(parameters)
> > >
> > >       modelMCMC <- buildMCMC(modelConf)

messages.body_plain:
Great, glad it helps.

On Tue, Aug 23, 2022 at 12:38 PM Quresh Latif <quresh...@birdconservancy.org> wrote:

> Ah, perfect! Thanks for pointing that out. I also see that you can set thinning when actually configuring the MCMC using the 'thin' argument (e.g., configureMCMC(Rmodel, thin = 10)). I don't see an argument for setting burn-in, but maybe I'm missing it? In any case, the option for setting thinning in the primary sampler is going to help a lot. Thank you!
>
> On Tuesday, August 23, 2022 at 10:24:59 AM UTC-6 db...@williams.edu wrote:
> > Quresh, just set the thinning interval in the MCMC configuration object (using conf$setThin(INTERVAL), I believe), doing that before you build and compile the MCMC.  Then, even using mcmc$run(ITERATIONS) will respect the thinning interval, and only record those samples internally.
> >
> > On Tue, Aug 23, 2022 at 12:17 PM Quresh Latif <quresh...@birdconservancy.org> wrote:
> > > One trade-off I am discovering with the above code is that because it uses the base function 'CModelMCMC$run' to allow resumption of sampling after checking convergence, I can't thin the samples as I go. I can thin after recovering the samples to save hard drive space, but the primary sampler does not allow thinning (or burn-in), which means that I end up running out of RAM before I reach convergence. For the time being, it seems like this code is useful at the initial stage of exploring a model, but once I have a sense of how long I'm going to need to run the sampler to get to convergence, I am probably going to have to switch to using the higher level 'nimbleMCMC' function, so that I can implement burn-in and thinning for better memory management.
> > >
> > > It might be nice for future versions of NIMBLE if either thinning/burn-in could be included in the base function (...$run) or if an option for resuming sampling could be incorporated into higher level functions that also allow thinning and burn-in.
> > >
> > > On Monday, August 15, 2022 at 11:23:43 AM UTC-6 Quresh Latif wrote:
> > > > Hello all. I realize this is an older post, but thought I'd share that I was able to successfully build on Adrian's code. The code below implements parallel processing, checks Rhats for specified parameters, and if they are too low, it keeps resuming until Rhats meet the desired threshold. The calculation of Rhats leverages the 'mcmcOutput' package. Perhaps others may find this useful.
> > > >
> > > >     #~~~~~~~~~Parallel processing code (won't work in Windows)~~~~~~~~~#
> > > >     library(parallel)
> > > >     library(coda)
> > > >     set.seed(3)
> > > >     cl<-makeCluster(nc, timeout = 5184000)
> > > >     clusterExport(cl, c("model", "inits", "data", "constants", "parameters", "ni"))
> > > >
> > > >     for (j in seq_along(cl)) {
> > > >       set.seed(j)
> > > >       init <- inits()
> > > >       clusterExport(cl[j], "init")
> > > >     }
> > > >     out1 <- clusterEvalQ(cl, {
> > > >       library(nimble)
> > > >       library(coda)
> > > >       model <- nimbleModel(code = model, name = "model",
> > > >
> > > >                            constants = constants, data = data,
> > > >
> > > >                            inits = init)
> > > >       Cmodel <- compileNimble(model)
> > > >       modelConf <- configureMCMC(model)
> > > >       modelConf$addMonitors(parameters)
> > > >
> > > >       modelMCMC <- buildMCMC(modelConf)
> > > >       CmodelMCMC <- compileNimble(modelMCMC, project = model)
> > > >       CmodelMCMC$run(ni, reset = FALSE)
> > > >       return(as.mcmc(as.matrix(CmodelMCMC$mvSamples)))
> > > >     })
> > > >
> > > >     ## Check convergence ##
> > > >     out2 <- out1
> > > >     out2[[1]] <- out2[[1]][seq(nb+2, ni+1, by = nt),]
> > > >     out2[[2]] <- out2[[2]][seq(nb+2, ni+1, by = nt),]
> > > >     out.mcmc <- coda::as.mcmc.list(lapply(out2, coda::as.mcmc))
> > > >     #traceplot(out.mcmc[, "b"])
> > > >     library(mcmcOutput)
> > > >     #if(nc > 1) mod.raw <- coda::as.mcmc.list(lapply(out$samples, coda::mcmc))
> > > >     mod <- mcmcOutput(out.mcmc)
> > > >     sumTab <- summary(mod, MCEpc = F, Rhat = T, n.eff = T, f = T, overlap0 = T, verbose = F)
> > > >     sumTab <- sumTab %>%
> > > >       as_tibble() %>%
> > > >       mutate(Parameter = row.names(sumTab)) %>%
> > > >       select(Parameter, mean:f)
> > > >     #MCMCvis::MCMCtrace(out.mcmc, params = "DELTA1[114, 2]", pdf = F, ISB = F)
> > > >     ind.Rht <- which(!str_detect(sumTab$Parameter, "test.n") &
> > > >                        !str_detect(sumTab$Parameter, "M.save") &
> > > >                        !str_detect(sumTab$Parameter, "pXtheta") &
> > > >                        !str_detect(sumTab$Parameter, "Ind") &
> > > >                        !str_detect(sumTab$Parameter, "ind"))
> > > >     mxRht <- sumTab %>% slice(ind.Rht) %>% pull(Rhat) %>% max(na.rm = T)
> > > >     #sumTab %>% slice(ind.Rht) %>% arrange(desc(Rhat)) %>% View()
> > > >
> > > >
> > > >     ## If has not converged, continue sampling
> > > >     n.reruns <- 0
> > > >     while(round(mxRht, digits = 1) > 1.1) {
> > > >       out2 <- clusterEvalQ(cl, {
> > > >         CmodelMCMC$run(ni, reset = FALSE)
> > > >         return(as.mcmc(as.matrix(CmodelMCMC$mvSamples)))
> > > >       })
> > > >
> > > >       n.reruns <- n.reruns + 1
> > > >       print(str_c("Reruns = ", n.reruns))
> > > >       if(n.reruns == 1) {
> > > >         nb2 <- nb + nb
> > > >         ni2 <- ni + ni
> > > >       } else {
> > > >         nb2 <- nb2 + nb
> > > >         ni2 <- ni2 + ni
> > > >       }
> > > >       out2[[1]] <- out2[[1]][seq(nb2+2, ni2+1, by = nt),]
> > > >       out2[[2]] <- out2[[2]][seq(nb2+2, ni2+1, by = nt),]
> > > >       out.mcmc.update <- coda::as.mcmc.list(lapply(out2, coda::as.mcmc))
> > > >
> > > >       mod <- mcmcOutput(out.mcmc.update)
> > > >       sumTab <- summary(mod, MCEpc = F, Rhat = T, n.eff = T, f = T, overlap0 = T, verbose = F)
> > > >       sumTab <- sumTab %>%
> > > >         as_tibble() %>%
> > > >         mutate(Parameter = row.names(sumTab)) %>%
> > > >         select(Parameter, mean:f)
> > > >       #MCMCvis::MCMCtrace(out.mcmc, params = "DELTA1[114, 2]", pdf = F, ISB = F)
> > > >       mxRht <- sumTab %>% slice(ind.Rht) %>% pull(Rhat) %>% max(na.rm = T)
> > > >       gc(verbose = F)
> > > >     }
> > > >     #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
> > > >
> > > > On Thursday, January 20, 2022 at 2:57:06 PM UTC-7 christophe...@gmail.com wrote:
> > > > > hi Dan,
> > > > >
> > > > > Thanks for commenting here.
> > > > >
> > > > > I've checked the example and I do get reproducible results using the code provided. I'm wondering if you modified it such that you are creating random initial values? If so, you'd need to use set.seed before you generate the initial values within the run_MCMC_allcode function.
> > > > >
> > > > > One other note is that the approach in that example relies on simply setting different seeds for the different chains. While this is probably safe, it is possible that the random numbers generated for one chain could partially overlap the random numbers generated for another chain. Even if this happened, I don't think it would cause substantive dependence between the chains. But your approach of using clusterSetRNGStream has the nice feature of ensuring the sequences of random numbers for each of the worker processes won't overlap.
> > > > >
> > > > > -chris
> > > > >
> > > > > On Tue, Jan 18, 2022 at 11:36 AM Daniel Eacker <taurusw...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > Hi,
> > > > > >
> > > > > > A bit late to add this, but I just wanted to add that I don't think this is correct for setting the seed in parallel processing using the parallel package:
> > > > > >
> > > > > > 1) In the `parLapply` call, the values of `X` are the values used for
> > > > > > the `seed` function. So it is used.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > I've tried this and it produces different results across MCMC simulations.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > What I've found that works for repeatable results using parallel processing is to add this just after making the cluster:
> > > > > >
> > > > > > e.g.,
> > > > > >
> > > > > > this_cluster <- makeCluster(2)
> > > > > >
> > > > > > clusterSetRNGStream(cl = this_cluster, 500) # note that 500 could be any integer.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > So, I don't think the X in parLapply actually does anything to produce repeatable results, whereas using this builtin function of the parallel package provides reproducible results.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Cheers,
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Dan
> > > > > >
> > > > > > On Thursday, April 2, 2020 at 11:39:15 AM UTC-8 db...@williams.edu wrote:
> > > > > > > To add just a few things:
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > 1) I'm not sure if there's any way to have the progress bar printed from one cluster node.  I agree, that would be nice.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > 2) Even if you return the compiled object(s) from one cluster (looping over clusterExport(), as was suggested), these compiled objects still could not be saved (to be reloaded subsequently into a new R session) due to the current nature of NIMBLE's compilation and the resulting objects.  As I believe was mentioned, addressing this is a long-term goal for NIMBLE.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > 3) Towards that end - being able to start a new R session, and resume executing an MCMC chain precisely where it left off - I wrote a vignette about "Saving Model and MCMC State", which demonstrates how to save the model and MCMC state after executing an MCMC algorithm. messages.body_plain:
Is it possible or are there plans to allow the user to pull the saved samples out of CModelMCMC and just keep the last sample along with mcmc parameters at that step (e.g., jump probabilities, etc.)? The idea would be to save the samples to the hard drive and keep on sampling without relying on RAM to store sampled iterations. This is what the `saveJAGS` package allows for JAGS, but JAGS is clearly a lot slower, so I'm wondering if there's any way to do this with NIMBLE.

On Tuesday, August 23, 2022 at 10:44:41 AM UTC-6 db...@williams.edu wrote:
> Great, glad it helps.
>
> On Tue, Aug 23, 2022 at 12:38 PM Quresh Latif <quresh...@birdconservancy.org> wrote:
> > Ah, perfect! Thanks for pointing that out. I also see that you can set thinning when actually configuring the MCMC using the 'thin' argument (e.g., configureMCMC(Rmodel, thin = 10)). I don't see an argument for setting burn-in, but maybe I'm missing it? In any case, the option for setting thinning in the primary sampler is going to help a lot. Thank you!
> >
> > On Tuesday, August 23, 2022 at 10:24:59 AM UTC-6 db...@williams.edu wrote:
> > > Quresh, just set the thinning interval in the MCMC configuration object (using conf$setThin(INTERVAL), I believe), doing that before you build and compile the MCMC.  Then, even using mcmc$run(ITERATIONS) will respect the thinning interval, and only record those samples internally.
> > >
> > > On Tue, Aug 23, 2022 at 12:17 PM Quresh Latif <quresh...@birdconservancy.org> wrote:
> > > > One trade-off I am discovering with the above code is that because it uses the base function 'CModelMCMC$run' to allow resumption of sampling after checking convergence, I can't thin the samples as I go. I can thin after recovering the samples to save hard drive space, but the primary sampler does not allow thinning (or burn-in), which means that I end up running out of RAM before I reach convergence. For the time being, it seems like this code is useful at the initial stage of exploring a model, but once I have a sense of how long I'm going to need to run the sampler to get to convergence, I am probably going to have to switch to using the higher level 'nimbleMCMC' function, so that I can implement burn-in and thinning for better memory management.
> > > >
> > > > It might be nice for future versions of NIMBLE if either thinning/burn-in could be included in the base function (...$run) or if an option for resuming sampling could be incorporated into higher level functions that also allow thinning and burn-in.
> > > >
> > > > On Monday, August 15, 2022 at 11:23:43 AM UTC-6 Quresh Latif wrote:
> > > > > Hello all. I realize this is an older post, but thought I'd share that I was able to successfully build on Adrian's code. The code below implements parallel processing, checks Rhats for specified parameters, and if they are too low, it keeps resuming until Rhats meet the desired threshold. The calculation of Rhats leverages the 'mcmcOutput' package. Perhaps others may find this useful.
> > > > >
> > > > >     #~~~~~~~~~Parallel processing code (won't work in Windows)~~~~~~~~~#
> > > > >     library(parallel)
> > > > >     library(coda)
> > > > >     set.seed(3)
> > > > >     cl<-makeCluster(nc, timeout = 5184000)
> > > > >     clusterExport(cl, c("model", "inits", "data", "constants", "parameters", "ni"))
> > > > >
> > > > >     for (j in seq_along(cl)) {
> > > > >       set.seed(j)
> > > > >       init <- inits()
> > > > >       clusterExport(cl[j], "init")
> > > > >     }
> > > > >     out1 <- clusterEvalQ(cl, {
> > > > >       library(nimble)
> > > > >       library(coda)
> > > > >       model <- nimbleModel(code = model, name = "model",
> > > > >
> > > > >                            constants = constants, data = data,
> > > > >
> > > > >                            inits = init)
> > > > >       Cmodel <- compileNimble(model)
> > > > >       modelConf <- configureMCMC(model)
> > > > >       modelConf$addMonitors(parameters)
> > > > >
> > > > >       modelMCMC <- buildMCMC(modelConf)
> > > > >       CmodelMCMC <- compileNimble(modelMCMC, project = model)
> > > > >       CmodelMCMC$run(ni, reset = FALSE)
> > > > >       return(as.mcmc(as.matrix(CmodelMCMC$mvSamples)))
> > > > >     })
> > > > >
> > > > >     ## Check convergence ##
> > > > >     out2 <- out1
> > > > >     out2[[1]] <- out2[[1]][seq(nb+2, ni+1, by = nt),]
> > > > >     out2[[2]] <- out2[[2]][seq(nb+2, ni+1, by = nt),]
> > > > >     out.mcmc <- coda::as.mcmc.list(lapply(out2, coda::as.mcmc))
> > > > >     #traceplot(out.mcmc[, "b"])
> > > > >     library(mcmcOutput)
> > > > >     #if(nc > 1) mod.raw <- coda::as.mcmc.list(lapply(out$samples, coda::mcmc))
> > > > >     mod <- mcmcOutput(out.mcmc)
> > > > >     sumTab <- summary(mod, MCEpc = F, Rhat = T, n.eff = T, f = T, overlap0 = T, verbose = F)
> > > > >     sumTab <- sumTab %>%
> > > > >       as_tibble() %>%
> > > > >       mutate(Parameter = row.names(sumTab)) %>%
> > > > >       select(Parameter, mean:f)
> > > > >     #MCMCvis::MCMCtrace(out.mcmc, params = "DELTA1[114, 2]", pdf = F, ISB = F)
> > > > >     ind.Rht <- which(!str_detect(sumTab$Parameter, "test.n") &
> > > > >                        !str_detect(sumTab$Parameter, "M.save") &
> > > > >                        !str_detect(sumTab$Parameter, "pXtheta") &
> > > > >                        !str_detect(sumTab$Parameter, "Ind") &
> > > > >                        !str_detect(sumTab$Parameter, "ind"))
> > > > >     mxRht <- sumTab %>% slice(ind.Rht) %>% pull(Rhat) %>% max(na.rm = T)
> > > > >     #sumTab %>% slice(ind.Rht) %>% arrange(desc(Rhat)) %>% View()
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > >     ## If has not converged, continue sampling
> > > > >     n.reruns <- 0
> > > > >     while(round(mxRht, digits = 1) > 1.1) {
> > > > >       out2 <- clusterEvalQ(cl, {
> > > > >         CmodelMCMC$run(ni, reset = FALSE)
> > > > >         return(as.mcmc(as.matrix(CmodelMCMC$mvSamples)))
> > > > >       })
> > > > >
> > > > >       n.reruns <- n.reruns + 1
> > > > >       print(str_c("Reruns = ", n.reruns))
> > > > >       if(n.reruns == 1) {
> > > > >         nb2 <- nb + nb
> > > > >         ni2 <- ni + ni
> > > > >       } else {
> > > > >         nb2 <- nb2 + nb
> > > > >         ni2 <- ni2 + ni
> > > > >       }
> > > > >       out2[[1]] <- out2[[1]][seq(nb2+2, ni2+1, by = nt),]
> > > > >       out2[[2]] <- out2[[2]][seq(nb2+2, ni2+1, by = nt),]
> > > > >       out.mcmc.update <- coda::as.mcmc.list(lapply(out2, coda::as.mcmc))
> > > > >
> > > > >       mod <- mcmcOutput(out.mcmc.update)
> > > > >       sumTab <- summary(mod, MCEpc = F, Rhat = T, n.eff = T, f = T, overlap0 = T, verbose = F)
> > > > >       sumTab <- sumTab %>%
> > > > >         as_tibble() %>%
> > > > >         mutate(Parameter = row.names(sumTab)) %>%
> > > > >         select(Parameter, mean:f)
> > > > >       #MCMCvis::MCMCtrace(out.mcmc, params = "DELTA1[114, 2]", pdf = F, ISB = F)
> > > > >       mxRht <- sumTab %>% slice(ind.Rht) %>% pull(Rhat) %>% max(na.rm = T)
> > > > >       gc(verbose = F)
> > > > >     }
> > > > >     #~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#

> > > > > On Thursday, January 20, 2022 at 2:57:06 PM UTC-7 christophe...@gmail.com wrote:

> > > > > > I've checked the example and I do get reproducible results using the code provided. I'm wondering if you modified it such that you are creating random initial values? If so, you'd need to use set.seed before you generate the initial values within the run_MCMC_allcode function.

While this is probably safe, it is possible that the random numbers generated for one chain could partially overlap the random numbers generated for another chain. Even if this happened, I don't think it would cause substantive dependence between the chains. But your approach of using clusterSetRNGStream has the nice feature of ensuring the sequences of random numbers for each of the worker processes won't overlap.
